title: perf-canary: add regression alert rules w/ dedup keys + severity mapping
author: Felix Schneider
body: Context: as part of the production perf-regression canary rollout, we need first-class alerting for p95 latency and tokens/sec regressions per (model, region, gpu_sku, scheduler_mode), with sane dedup/grouping and a severity policy that won’t immediately melt pagers during phase 1. This PR adds the initial set of Prometheus/Alertmanager rule definitions in observability-pack (plus rule-test fixtures) and aligns labeling with the metric spec + SRE routing conventions. What’s included: 1) New regression alert rules for perf-canary. - perf_canary_p95_latency_regression: fires when canary p95 latency exceeds baseline by threshold for a sustained period (see thresholds below). - perf_canary_tokens_per_sec_regression: fires when tokens/sec drops below baseline by threshold for a sustained period. - perf_canary_signal_quality_low (ticket-only): detects low sample size / missing slices so we don’t page on unreliable windows. 2) Dedup keys and grouping policy. - Alerts are keyed to: alertname + model + region + gpu_sku + scheduler_mode + metric (latency|tps) + canary_mode (streaming|non-streaming). - Explicitly NOT included: runtime_build / git_sha (too volatile; causes dedup churn). These are included as annotations for context, not grouping labels. - Dedup also includes canary_workload_id only when present (to isolate future workload expansions without exploding cardinality). 3) Severity mapping (phase 1 defaults). - severity=page (PagerDuty): latency regression >= +12% OR tps regression <= -10% for 20m, and signal_quality=good. - severity=ticket (#eng-runtime + Jira/Linear follow-up): latency regression >= +7% OR tps regression <= -6% for 30m. - severity=info: signal-quality issues / partial slice gaps (no paging). These numbers are intentionally conservative for phase 1; ENG-2855 backtesting suggests these levels keep pages under ~1/day in us-east on 2–3 models while still catching the obvious regressions. 4) Maintenance window / deploy suppression hooks. - Rules honor the standard suppression label (maintenance_suppressed="true") when present on the underlying time series (produced by the regression-detector pipeline / slo-toolkit helper). - Added explicit annotations + links so that during deploy windows responders can see that suppression was active, rather than wondering why graphs moved without alerts. 5) Alert payload enrichment. - Added annotations: dashboard_url, runbook_url, baseline_window (7d rolling median), baseline_value, current_value, percent_delta, last_deploy_event (if available), plus a canned "What to check first" snippet (queue depth, gpu_sku split, recent runtime deploy). - Payload is designed to match incident-bot formatting (see incident-bot PR 233) and to make it obvious which slice is affected. Implementation details: - Using recording rules already produced by the perf-canary pipeline: perf_canary:latency_p95_ms{...} and perf_canary:tokens_per_sec{...} along with perf_canary:regression_ratio{metric="latency_p95_ms"|"tokens_per_sec"} and perf_canary:signal_quality_ok. - Alerts are expressed in Jsonnet to keep parity with the existing observability-pack rule generation. - Rule tests cover: (a) no-alert when under min sample size, (b) correct dedup labels, (c) page vs ticket thresholds, and (d) suppression behavior. Files changed (high level): - alerts/perf_canary/perf_canary_regressions.libsonnet: main alert definitions + templates. - alerts/perf_canary/perf_canary_recording_rules.libsonnet: small helper recording rules for percent_delta + baseline/current annotations. - alertmanager/routes/perf_canary_routes.libsonnet: routing rules for severity=page to SRE PD service with team hint runtime-oncall; severity=ticket to Slack + issue creation hook. - tests/perf_canary_regression_alerts_test.yaml: promtool rule tests w/ fixtures for latency/tps regressions. - docs/alerts/perf-canary.md: responder-facing notes (links to runbook; what fields to expect). Notes / trade-offs: - runtime_build is intentionally excluded from grouping labels after SRE review; it will create one alert per deploy and breaks dedup on rollouts. We still include runtime_build and git_sha as annotations (best-effort) to speed up attribution. - We keep scheduler_mode as a label because it’s a small bounded set and is directly useful for triage (pinning vs experimental). If scheduler_mode label becomes high-cardinality due to new experiments, we should revisit. - During phase 1 we page SRE first (per ENG-2848), but we attach team_hint=runtime so incident-bot can auto-suggest the right SME channel / assign on confirmation. Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Add model-specific thresholds once we have enough stable baseline data per model family (ENG-2855 tuning). - Add GPU fleet heterogeneity guardrails (e.g., require split-by-gpu_sku coverage before paging). - Add automatic links to recent runtime PRs once deploy annotations are fully wired end-to-end (waiting on release metadata propagation).
commits: alerts: add perf-canary regression alert definitions + templates
alertmanager: route perf-canary alerts by severity with stable grouping keys
tests: add promtool rule tests for latency/tps regressions and suppression
docs: perf-canary alert payload fields + responder notes
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please don’t include runtime_build in any grouping labels; it’ll dedup-churn every rollout. Suggest: keep it as an annotation only, and ensure the dedup key is (model, region, gpu_sku, scheduler_mode, canary_mode, metric). Also can we bump the 'for' to 20m for page severity to reduce noise during cache warmups?

Felix Schneider (author): Ack on runtime_build—moved to annotations only and updated rule tests to ensure it’s not in labels. Increased page severity 'for' to 20m; ticket severity kept at 30m. Added a signal_quality gate so we don’t fire on low sample windows.

Tomáš Novák (SRE): The thresholds look aggressive for paging given this is phase 1. Can we start ticket-first for 7% latency / 6% tps, and page only at 12% / 10%? Also please add an explicit maintenance suppression check (maintenance_suppressed="true") so deploy windows don’t page.

Felix Schneider (author): Updated per your suggestion: ticket thresholds at 7%/6%, page at 12%/10%. Added suppression condition + annotation noting when suppressed. Linked to runbook section about deploy windows.

Rafael Mendes (SRE): Routing: please set pager_team=sre and team_hint=runtime, and ensure the alertname is stable across metrics. We also need a single dedup key for Alertmanager grouping so incident-bot doesn’t post duplicates to #eng-oncall.

Felix Schneider (author): Added pager_team and team_hint labels. Consolidated alertnames to perf_canary_regression with metric label (latency|tps) so grouping is consistent. Dedup key now stable and covered by tests.

Allison Grant (Observability standards): +1 overall. One nit: label names should match the metric spec (gpu_sku, scheduler_mode, region). Also make sure we’re not introducing any unbounded labels (workload_id should be optional + sanitized).
Felix Schneider (author): Renamed labels to match spec and gated workload_id behind a whitelist (empty by default).
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Approved after changes. Please monitor page volume in phase 1 and be ready to tune (ENG-2855).
Tomáš Novák (SRE): Approved. The signal_quality alert should be ticket-only (no PD). Good to merge.
release_notes: Internal: added perf-canary regression alert rules (latency p95 + tokens/sec) with stable dedup keys, severity mapping, maintenance suppression support, and rule-test coverage.
